turns.content: For an ideal gas with temperature-dependent molar heat capacity, derive the entropy change for n moles taken from (T_i,P_i) to (T_f,P_f). Use the ideal-gas value of the thermal expansion coefficient in Eq. (5.23). The sample considered below contains 2.50 mol of CO2.
For CO2, C_{P,m}/(J mol^-1 K^-1)=18.86+7.937e-2(T/K)-6.7834e-5(T/K)^2+2.4426e-8(T/K)^3. Integrate C_{P,m}/T analytically to obtain the molar temperature contribution.
Evaluate that molar enthalpy temperature-integral contribution between T_i=450 K and T_f=800 K.
Evaluate the molar pressure contribution for compression from P_i=1.35 bar to P_f=3.45 bar, using R=8.314 J mol^-1 K^-1.
Combine the relevant molar enthalpy contributions and use n=2.50 mol to calculate Delta S for the CO2 sample.
Explain the sign of the pressure contribution and how it modifies the positive entropy change from heating.
Check the calculation by describing an equivalent reversible two-step path and verify that the temperature and pressure terms correspond to those two steps.
Report the total entropy change in J K^-1 and summarize the contributions that determine it.
